diag.title: Diagnostics (read-only)
diag.intro: Lets the AI of the chat and investigations check the actual state of your infrastructure itself (containers, disk, memory, services) instead of asking you to run docker ps or df. Everything is read-only: nothing can be started, stopped or changed.
diag.docker_hint: Through a Docker socket proxy that only allows reads (state, health, restarts, logs, usage). Sentinel never mounts the socket itself.
diag.docker_compose_hint: Add this service to the same docker-compose.yml as Sentinel, then run docker compose up -d. The address http://docker-proxy:2375 is already filled in.
diag.unraid_step1: In the Unraid terminal, create a dedicated network (once): docker network create sentinel. To see it in the network list, enable Settings › Docker › Preserve user defined networks.
diag.unraid_step2: In the Apps tab, install dockersocket (IBRACORP) and pick the sentinel network. Keep CONTAINERS=1 and POST=0.
diag.unraid_step3: Edit the Log-to-LLM-Sentinel container and pick the sentinel network too.
diag.unraid_step4: The address http://dockersocket:2375 is filled in: click Test and save.
diag.unraid_no_port: Do not publish the proxy port on your network: even read-only, it exposes the configuration of all your containers.
diag.host_hint: An SSH key generated by Sentinel, allowed on the server only for a script of read-only checks (disk, memory, load, network shares, services). Even if stolen, it allows nothing else.
diag.regenerate_confirm: The old key will stop working: you will need to paste the block on the server again. Continue?
diag.step_install: Paste this block in a terminal on the server.
diag.step_settings: Check the server address and the user shown at the end of the block, then click Test and save.
diag.script_outdated: ⚠ Connected, but the script installed on the server is outdated: paste the step 2 block again to get the latest checks.
diag.delete_confirm: Delete this connection? The AI will no longer have access to it.
diag.err_name_taken: This name is taken: the AI refers to connections by name.
diag.err_url: The address must start with http:// or https://.
diag.need_host: Enter the server address and the user.
diag.install_review: To review it: the header sums up what it does, only the numbered steps change the server, and everything after them is the read-only checks script, commented check by check.
diag.remove_hint: Paste this block in a terminal on the server (platform chosen in step 2): it removes Sentinel's key and the script, so Sentinel can no longer connect. Then forget the server in Sentinel.
diag.forget_confirm: Clear the address and user? The AI will no longer have access to the server.
diag.web_hint: For the chat and investigations only. Queries go to public search engines: Sentinel refuses those containing an address, a path or the name of one of your machines. Automatic alert analysis never has access to it.
diag.web_compose_hint: Sentinel's compose file already contains this service, with no published port. Start it with docker compose --profile web up -d, then keep the suggested address.
diag.web_unraid_step2: In its settings.yml, usually under /mnt/user/appdata/searxng/, add json under search: formats:, next to html. Without it, SearXNG answers 403.
diag.web_unraid_step4: Enter its address here, for example http://SERVER-IP:8080, or http://searxng:8080 if it is on the same Docker network as Sentinel.
diag.key_paste_hint: OpenSSH private key with no passphrase, for example the one from an earlier Sentinel install. It stays in Sentinel and is never shown again.
diag.key_imported: Key saved. Paste the block on the server again if it is not already allowed there.
diag.account_hint: Change it before copying the block. If this account already exists and was not created by Sentinel, the block stops without changing anything.
diag.web_engines: Many search engines block home addresses: the test shows which ones really answer from your connection.
diag.cve_hint: When an alert cites a CVE, Sentinel shows its official sheet: active exploitation (CISA's KEV catalog), affected versions, score. Only the CVE number is sent to NVD. The sheet informs and never changes the severity: a log line can cite any CVE.
diag.web_blocked: The instance answers, but no engine returns results for now (no answer: {failed}). They often block for a while: try again later.
diag.web_paused: Searches suspended for {n} more min: no engine answered ({engines}). Insisting would prolong the block. Test resumes as soon as an engine answers.
diag.web_full: Limit reached: {n} searches this hour. The AI will resume once the hour has passed.

sources.docker_step1: Sentinel reads a container's logs through a read-only Docker proxy. It has access to nothing else and cannot change anything. You can reuse the diagnostics proxy.
sources.docker_step2: Choose the connection, then the container to watch. One rule per container.
sources.docker_step3: Reading starts when the rule is saved. After a restart, of Sentinel or of the container, it resumes where it stopped.

sources.docker_setup: Set it up in a new tab
sources.hass_step1: In Home Assistant, open your profile (your name, bottom left), Security tab, then Long-lived access tokens > Create token. The account must be an administrator.
sources.hass_step2: Paste the token below with the Home Assistant address, then click Test.
sources.hass_step3: That's all: no automation to install. Sentinel receives warnings and errors, stack traces included; Home Assistant does not publish other levels through this channel.
sources.hass_test_ok: Connected to Home Assistant {version}. {n} entries in its log.
sources.mqtt_step1: Enter the address of your MQTT server (Mosquitto, the Home Assistant add-on…) and its credentials if it asks for them, then click Test: Sentinel listens for 3 seconds and shows the active topics.
sources.mqtt_step2: Choose what to follow. + replaces one level, # replaces everything after it: zigbee2mqtt/#, tele/+/LWT.
sources.mqtt_step3: Each line received starts with its topic. Retained messages are ignored: they are old states, not events. Avoid # alone, it is often very chatty.
sources.mqtt_test_topics: Connected. {n} active topic(s) seen in 3 seconds:
sources.mqtt_test_ok: Connected. No message seen in 3 seconds.
sources.shipper_title: Send from a log shipper (Fluent Bit, Alloy, OpenTelemetry, Windows logs)
sources.shipper_intro: Machines already equipped with a log shipper? Add this rule as a destination, instead of or on top of what you use. Every line sent arrives here.
sources.shipper_fluentbit_hint: Fluent Bit, on Linux: add this to fluent-bit.conf. Replace the path with your logs.
sources.shipper_windows_hint: Install Fluent Bit for Windows and put this in its fluent-bit.conf: the System and Application logs arrive here.
sources.shipper_alloy_hint: Grafana Alloy: add this to its configuration. Replace the path with your logs.
sources.shipper_otel_hint: OpenTelemetry Collector: add this exporter to your logs pipeline. Your applications keep sending to the collector.
sources.cfg_hint: A connection serves every rule that needs it. Docker logs use the connections of the Diagnostics tab.
sources.mqtt_listening: Listening to the MQTT server for 3 seconds…
sources.mqtt_seen: {n} topic(s) seen in 3 seconds. Click to choose:
sources.mqtt_seen_none: No message seen in 3 seconds: type the topic to follow.
